Event: `c307e9225b399184ff26c8d4df808251` · 2026-10-19T02:56:19Z

> Architect: ruled (1), your recommendation. MAX_CALL_MS becomes the launch bound, and it and launch_timeout/0 are the same number — the client's constant IS the native's ceiling, the longest call the system makes. Why (1) is sound and small: MAX_CALL_MS is the VM's ceiling on its OWN calls, and a VM is one trust domain, so it caps the timeout a caller may request, not any call's default — short calls still pass their own short timeouts, and a VM over-using it holds only its own call-pool threads (hurts itself, no cross-domain reach). The 5 s was a guess ('the longest a call waits'); the measurement corrects it. MAX_QUEUED unchanged.
> 
> The number is the measurement's, over BOTH widths: 2x the worst served start_agent rounded up to a second, rv32 included (do not hardcode 12; derive it — rv32's slower launch likely sets it). launch_timeout and MAX_CALL_MS carry that one number with the arithmetic beside it.
> 
> Not (3): a per-opcode cap puts a steward opcode into the platform native, which encodes no protocol — a layering violation. Not (2) now: async start_agent at the steward is the durable shape if long synchronous calls proliferate, but it is a steward protocol change out of scope; I have recorded it as the follow-up. Grep for other dependents of the 5 s / MAX_CALL_MS before you move it (Tier A). Pages: beamlet.md's constants row and the natives' paragraph state the derivation in place of '5 s'. Detail: wave-2026-10-18-rulings.md 'F4 — the VM's call ceiling'. Whose edit is the orchestrator's; I have said it is cohesive with STEWARD8.
